# Katahdin (01, engineer) — BAD-090

## Brief
Take the collab sync loop down to **one `info` read per cycle** on both clients, without making anyone wait longer to see a collaborator's take.

## Where this comes from

BAD-080 (PR #386) took the `info` read off the *push* path, because a read is what completes a wrapping room's wrap and the pusher was wrapping the room under its own take. BAD-089 (#387) then made the shared hold predicate one definition. This ticket is the last of that family: `pullTakes()` still opens with an `info` of its own, and `runCollabSync` then calls `refreshCollab` for a second one. Two reads per cycle, per member — with 8 members on a 60s poll that is 16 reads a minute for a room instead of 8.

BAD-080 deliberately left `pullTakes` alone: it was not in that ticket's scope, and a pull is not a delivery.

## The thing the ticket does not say, and which is the whole design

**Do not just copy `pushTakes`'s fix into `pullTakes`.** The two have different consequences for a stale snapshot, and this is the part to get right:

- For a **push**, deciding from a stale snapshot can only *delay* — you send on the next cycle. BAD-080 documented that cost and accepted it.
- For a **pull**, deciding from a stale snapshot means **not downloading a take that already exists on the server** until the next cycle. `collab.info` is refreshed by `refreshCollab` at the *tail* of the previous sync, so at pull time it is up to a full poll period old. Folding naively would systematically add up to ~60s of latency to seeing other people's takes — a real regression in the thing collab is for, traded for bandwidth nobody complained about.

So the question to settle before writing anything is **ordering**, not sourcing. The obvious candidate: take the one read at the *front* of the cycle and let both push and pull decide from that single fresh snapshot, dropping the trailing `refreshCollab` read. That would be one read, fresh, and would make the ticket's "ordering nobody has written down" into a stated invariant.

Before you do that, work out **what the trailing `refreshCollab` is actually for** — I have not traced it and you must. Candidates: it reflects post-push state in the UI (the room's own takes list, the cast strip, the phase), it is what lands a just-claimed seat, and `renderIfCollabOpen`/`renderBoothCollab` may depend on it having run. If moving it to the front loses something the UI needs *after* the writes, then say so and propose the alternative you can defend — including "one read at the front and keep a cheap trailing one only when the cycle actually wrote something", or "this ticket should not be done as stated". A well-argued `member block` with the trace in it is a better outcome than a clever change that makes the room stale.

**Do not regress BAD-080.** Whatever you do, a client mid-delivery must still make no read: `collabTakeInFlight()` / `collabIdleBeat` and the focus-poll gates stay exactly as they are, and moving a read to the front of the cycle must not put one inside a delivery window. `test/collabdelivery.test.js` is the pin — if your change makes one of its assertions need rewording, stop and look hard at why.

## Both clients

This is one rule in two places and they must agree — BAD-089 exists because they drifted once already.

- **Web**: `web/collabweb-sync.js` — `pullTakes()` opens with `collabFetch('info', …)` and feeds `info.data.takes` to `CollabRules.pendingPulls`; `runCollabSync()` calls `refreshCollab(state.pack, { pull: false })` at the tail.
- **Desktop**: `main.js` `collab:pull` does the same shape; `renderer/app.js` drives the cadence and `refreshCollab` there.

If a piece of the decision belongs in `src/collab.js` next to `takeInFlight`, put it there rather than writing it twice — that is now the established home.

**Scope note:** the desktop half of this repo is currently deferred work (`.claude/skills/deferring-desktop-work`), but a ticket spanning both clients is not split, and Eric asked for this one directly. Do both halves so they cannot drift.

## Ticket proposals
- **refreshCollab's supersession guard silently cancels the arrival pull, and nobody retries it** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-093]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: BAD-090 kept the sync's pull out from under this guard, but refreshCollab(pack, {pull:true}) still runs its own pull below it, and that path is how a scene ARRIVES in a room. onSceneSelected/selectPack fires it un-awaited; if the 20s focus poll, openCollabModal, a seat claim or a collab:changed event bumps collab.seq in the window between the read and the pull, the arrival pull is abandoned with no retry and no error, and the superseding refresh passes pull:false so it fetches nothing. The person who just opened a collab scene sees an empty room for up to 60s. autoPullWrapped is worse: it is once per room per run (collabAutoPulled guards it), so its single pull being superseded means the wrapped room's takes wait on the poll with no second attempt. The fix is probably to say in refreshCollab what BAD-090 said in runCollabSync — supersession cancels the PAINT, not the TRANSFER — by running the pull before the seq check and gating only the toast and the renders on it. That needs web/collabweb-model.js, which was outside BAD-090's deliverables.
  Evidence: web/collabweb-model.js:203 is the guard ('if (seq !== collab.seq || ...) return false;'), :224-228 is the pull branch below it. renderer/app.js:4759 and :4786-4790 are the same pair. Callers that bump the seq without pulling: web/collabweb.js:136 (20s focus poll), web/collabweb-modal.js:69, web/collabweb-tab.js:213, web/collabweb-seat.js:60/87/101, renderer/app.js:4876 (focus poll) and :4897. BAD-090's test/collabreads.test.js reproduces the identical mechanism for the sync path ('a focus poll landing mid-cycle does not cancel the cycle`s pull') — that test fails on the folded version with wire 'upload-url -> commit -> info -> info' and an empty remote store. Found by BADS-090/Desiree.
- **main pushes a room's collab:changed diff before the status reply the renderer is awaiting** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-094]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: main.js's collab:status handler calls collabPushChanged(events) and THEN returns the status. A webContents.send is delivered to the renderer before the invoke reply resolves, so the renderer reacts to a room's news while the very call that produced it is still outstanding. onCollabChanged then fires refreshCollab, which bumps collab.seq and can supersede the refresh that is still in flight. BAD-090 had to route around this (the sync pulls outside refreshCollab rather than inside it) and named it in renderer/CLAUDE.md, but the ordering itself is untouched and will bite the next thing that assumes an invoke reply lands before its side effects. Worth either deferring the push to a microtask after the reply is returned, or having onCollabChanged skip a room whose status call is still outstanding. Neither is BAD-090's business and neither should be done without deciding which of the two is the real rule.
  Evidence: main.js:3556-3558 (the absorbCollabInfo + collabPushChanged pair inside ipcMain.handle('collab:status')). src/collab.js diffCollabInfo emits part_progress exactly when another member's take count rises, so the read that FIRST sees a collaborator's take is the one that fires the event. renderer/app.js:6389 onCollabChanged -> refreshCollab(pack, {pull:false}) -> ++collab.seq. BADS-090/Desiree confirmed the delivery order with a minimal Electron experiment: ORDER:[changed-listener, status-reply]. Related and smaller: absorbCollabInfo (main.js:4453) has no monotonicity guard, so a pollCollabInfosOnce info fetch already in flight when collab:status absorbs will overwrite the newer snapshot when it resolves — now that collab:pull decides from that store, worst case is one take one cycle late.

## Result
DONE, uncommitted in the worktree. One info read per sync cycle on both clients, with the pull's latency and BAD-080 both intact.

WHAT THE TRAILING refreshCollab IS FOR (traced, since the brief asked): three jobs, and only ONE is a read. (1) its info/collab:status, (2) collab.remote = listRemoteTakes / collab:takes then resolveCollabTakes + repaint + startCollabPolling, (3) dropPin on 403/404/closed and the clock skew. Jobs 2 and 3 are local or cheap; nothing the UI needs after a cycle's writes comes from the server. That is what made the READ movable.

WHAT I LANDED. The cycle is: push (no read) -> the trailing refreshCollab, now the cycle's only read -> the pull, deciding from the snapshot that read just left, outside the refresh. Web: pullTakes() drops its own info and decides from collab.info with pushTakes's same 'no snapshot' bootstrap; runCollabSync does refreshCollab(pull:false) then pulls itself and re-runs the local tail. Desktop: main's collab:pull decides from collabInfoSnaps (the store collab:push uses) with the same bootstrap; renderer's runCollabSync the same shape. src/collab.js unchanged - the piece that differs between push and pull is an ORDERING, not a predicate, so there was nothing to share there.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT take the read to the front of the cycle: that puts info -> upload-url -> PUT -> commit on the wire, byte-for-byte the sequence BAD-080 deleted.

THE BLOCKER I FIRST SHIPPED, found by the reviewer child (Desiree) and fixed: my first cut folded the pull into refreshCollab's own pull branch, which sits BELOW that function's 'seq !== collab.seq' guard, so any concurrent refreshCollab(pull:false) cancelled it and none of those callers pulls. Systematic on desktop (main pushes collab:changed before the invoke reply, from the very read that first sees the take). Reproduced, then fixed by keeping the pull in runCollabSync where it was never seq-gated - supersession behaviour is now exactly what it was before this ticket.

COUNTED, NOT ARGUED (test/collabreads.test.js, a second vm harness that loads the REAL refreshCollab from collabweb-model.js and records at Api.supa). BEFORE: 'upload-url -> commit -> info -> download-url -> info' = 2; scene-select refresh 'info -> info' = 2. AFTER: 'upload-url -> commit -> info -> download-url' = 1; scene-select 1. Ran the same tests against a NAIVE fold: it reaches 1 read and fails 4 assertions including both latency ones - so a count-only test would have passed the regression.

VERIFIED: npm test 1846/1724 pass/0 fail/122 skip, exit 0 (baseline 1836/1714/0/122; the 10 new are mine, skips unchanged). SMOKE_SCOPE=booth npm run smoke SMOKE_OK exit 0, booth screenshot clean. test/collabdelivery.test.js untouched, 15/15 pass. Web page served from this worktree on 8901: all collabweb-*.js and src/collab.js 200, and the live page confirms pullTakes opens with no read while runCollabSync owns its pull.
